newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares lower, flail for direction.
newsitem.headline: German shares lower, flail for direction.

text.p: German shares were likely to remain rangebound in the near future, contaminated by uncertainty about the next likely direction of global markets and the outlook for the dollar.
"We just don't have a direction," said one dealer. "I would view this as a mild consolidation phase, nothing significant."
The 30-share IBIS DAX index was down 29.38 points at 3,174.41 points at 1341 GMT, around ten points below the close of floor trading.
March DTB DAX futures were down 30.5 points at 3,184 points, still holding above a support level at 3,180.
The weaker dollar was pressuring the market and dealers said many investors were keeping out of the market before Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's speech on Wednesday.
"This development is healthy," one share dealer said. "If the bond markets don't go mad shares should soon find their feet again."
Attention will be fixed on what Greenspan has to say about U.S. stock market market activity, especially since previous comments about the market briefly interrupted its advance.
Steel and engineering group Thyssen bucked an otherwise firmly downward trend after a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell upgrade.

Thyssen was just off intraday highs at 328.50 marks, up 8.60 marks in the afternoon, after Deutsche MG said it raised its recommendation to overweight from neutral and said it expected the shares to hit 400 marks over the next year or two.
Dollar-sensitive chemical and engineering companies were under most pressure from the decline in the dollar, which fell more than a pfennig against the mark.
Shares in chemicals group Hoechst AG fell 1.45 marks to 70.15 marks.
